messages:
maria: quick design sync : proposing a small severity pill on eval scorecard rows to help triage regressions (tiny color dot + short label). want to avoid clutter in dense lists.

jon: I like the signal, but color-only is risky. suggest color + 1char glyph (e.g., ! for critical) and a11y text. also how does this interact with compact rows?

ash: compact mode should drop text and show outline-only dot with tooltip on hover/focus. in expanded rows show label + short reason like 'Critical: failing assertions'.

maria: copy options: short visible text = 'Critical' / 'Notice' / 'Info'. tooltip: full reason + numbers. keep visible text minimal to avoid biasing reviewers.

a11y-bot: accessibility: provide aria-label on the pill with full explanation and ensure tooltip content is referenced via aria-describedby. add aria-live update when pinned/toggled counts change. example: aria-label="Critical regression: 3 failing assertions".

jon: keyboard affordance: when filtering to criticals, Tab should land on first pill and Enter/Space opens diff details. show small "Press Space to open" hint on focus.

ash: bulk behavior: allow filtering to severity and bulk-flag for follow-up. bulk modal should show sampling preview and counts, not auto-approve. CTA 'Flag selected (N)'.

maria: analytics to emit: severity_shown, severity_filtered, bulk_flag_applied. product-analytics will need severity in payload.

jon: dev note: auto-approve rules must ignore rows marked Critical. ui should show banner: "Auto-approve paused: X criticals". copy needs to be explicit.

a11y-bot: test checklist additions: tooltip reachable by keyboard, aria-describedby present, aria-live announces pinned counts, contrast >= 4.5:1 for small text.

maria: action items: 1) quick mock of compact vs expanded pill (jon) 2) tooltip + aria copy (ash) 3) add acceptance tests and analytics events (maria). I'll post mocks later today.

jon: will mock and include hover/focus states.

ash: will write aria snippets and keyboard handlers.

maria: thanks all  will follow up after mocks.
